title: Nafaa API
summary: Read products, stock, customers, sales and online orders from your Nafaa business, create customers, and get signed webhooks when something happens. REST over HTTPS with JSON, authenticated with an API key you create in Settings, Developer.

blocks.markdown:
The Nafaa API is a REST API at `https://api.nafaa.pk/api/v1`. Every request is authenticated with an API key from **Settings → Developer** in the Nafaa app, sent as a bearer token. Responses are JSON.

## What you can do

- Read **products** (by id, SKU or barcode), **stock** by branch, **customers**, **sales** and **online orders**.
- Create a **customer** with a write key; the same phone number returns the existing customer.
- Subscribe to **webhooks** such as `sale.created` or `stock.low`, which Zapier and Make can use as REST hooks.

## Your first request

`GET /v1/me` tells you which business a key belongs to, so it is the quickest way to test a key.

tabs.label: JavaScript

tabs.code:
import os, requests

res = requests.get(
    'https://api.nafaa.pk/api/v1/me',
    headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.environ['NAFAA_API_KEY']}"},
)
print(res.json())
tabs.label: Python

blocks.markdown:
## Pagination

List endpoints take `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `page` (from 1), and return `{ data, page, limit, hasMore }`. Keep asking for the next page while `hasMore` is true. Use `updated_since` (an ISO date) to fetch only what changed since your last sync.

## Limits

Each key can make 120 requests a minute. A key can be limited to one branch; it then only sees that branch's data.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/v1/me` | The business the key belongs to |
| GET | `/v1/products`, `/v1/products/{id}` | Products; one by id, SKU or barcode |
| GET | `/v1/stock` | Stock by product and branch |
| GET | `/v1/customers`, `/v1/customers/{id}` | Customers |
| POST | `/v1/customers` | Create a customer (write key) |
| GET | `/v1/sales`, `/v1/sales/{id}` | Sales; one by id or sale number |
| GET | `/v1/orders`, `/v1/orders/{id}` | Online orders |
| GET, POST, DELETE | `/v1/webhooks…` | Webhook events and subscriptions |

title: Authentication
summary: Create an API key in Settings, Developer and send it as a bearer token on every request. Read keys can list data; write keys can also create customers. Keys can be limited to one branch and revoked at any time.

blocks.markdown:
Create a key in the Nafaa app under **Settings → Developer**. Keys start with `nfk_`. Store them in a secret manager or an environment variable, never in a browser app.

Send the key in the `Authorization` header on every request:

```http
GET /api/v1/products HTTP/1.1
Host: api.nafaa.pk
Authorization: Bearer nfk_your_key
```

## Scopes

- **Read** keys can call every `GET` endpoint and manage webhooks.
- **Write** keys can also create customers with `POST /v1/customers`.

A missing or wrong key returns `401`. Revoke a key in Settings → Developer and it stops working at once.

title: Products
summary: GET /v1/products returns your products page by page, with search and updated_since filters. GET /v1/products/{id} finds a single product by its id, SKU or barcode, which is handy when a scanner or another system only knows the code.

blocks.markdown: Returns products in pages. Filter by name with `search`, or use `updated_since` to sync only products changed since your last run (results then come oldest change first).

title: Stock
summary: GET /v1/stock returns the stock of every product in every branch, with its low-stock alert level and an isLow flag, so another system can mirror your stock or raise reorders. Filter by branch with shop_id and by change time with updated_since.

blocks.markdown: Each row is one product in one branch: `productId`, `variantId`, `shopId`, `name`, `sku`, `barcode`, `unit`, `stock`, `lowStockAlert`, `isLow` and `updatedAt`. Rows come oldest change first, so `updated_since` gives you a simple incremental sync.

title: Customers
summary: GET /v1/customers lists customers with search, phone and updated_since filters, and GET /v1/customers/{id} returns one. POST /v1/customers creates a customer with a write key; if the phone number already exists, the existing customer is returned instead of a duplicate.

blocks.markdown: Create a customer with `name` and `phone`, plus optional `email`, `city`, `address` and `notes`. Phone numbers are matched on their last ten digits, so `0300 1234567` and `+92 300 1234567` find the same customer.

title: Sales and online orders
summary: GET /v1/sales lists counter and online sales, and GET /v1/orders lists online orders from your website, Shopify, WooCommerce, Daraz and other channels. Both take from, to, status and updated_since filters, and each has an endpoint to fetch one record by id.

blocks.markdown:
Filter by date with `from` and `to`, by `status`, and by `shop_id` for one branch. `GET /v1/sales/{id}` also accepts the sale number printed on the receipt.

For live updates, subscribe to `sale.created` and the `online_order.*` [webhooks](/developers/webhooks) instead of polling.

title: Webhooks
summary: Subscribe a URL to events such as sale.created, customer.created, online order updates and stock.low. Every delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 so you can verify it came from Nafaa, and a sample endpoint returns real example payloads for tools like Zapier.

blocks.markdown:
Subscribe with `POST /v1/webhooks` and a body of `{ "url": "https://example.com/hooks/nafaa", "events": ["sale.created"] }`. `GET /v1/webhooks/events` lists every event, `GET /v1/webhooks/sample/{type}` returns an example payload, and `DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}` unsubscribes.

## Events

`sale.created`, `customer.created`, `online_order.created`, `online_order.accepted`, `online_order.dispatched`, `online_order.delivered`, `online_order.cancelled`, `online_order.returned` and `stock.low`.

## Verifying a delivery

Each request carries `X-Nafaa-Event`, `X-Nafaa-Delivery` (the event id; ignore repeats), `X-Nafaa-Timestamp` and `X-Nafaa-Signature: t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex>`. The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of `<timestamp>.<raw body>` with your webhook secret.
